insider_note: This is the easiest of the three tan(x/2) questions on this page — the (1+t²) cancels AND the remaining quadratic in t factors immediately into (1+t), with no completing the square needed at all.

steps.label: Set up the tan(x/2) substitution
steps.why: The same universal substitution as answer 21 — it works on any rational function of sinx and cosx, including one with a constant term (the 1) added in, as here.
common_mistakes: Misremembering the sign inside (1−t²) for cosx.
Forgetting to also convert the constant 1 to (1+t²)/(1+t²) before combining terms.
steps.memory_tip: Constants need the same denominator (1+t²) as sinx and cosx before they can be combined.

steps.label: Substitute and simplify
steps.why: Writing the constant 1 with the common denominator (1+t²) lets t² cancel completely against −t², leaving the linear (2+2t) — no quadratic survives in this particular denominator.
common_mistakes: Not combining all three terms over the common denominator (1+t²) before adding.
Missing that +t² and −t² cancel, and instead carrying a leftover t² term into later work.
steps.memory_tip: 1 + sinx + cosx always simplifies to a LINEAR expression in t, never a quadratic — the t² terms cancel here.

steps.label: Integrate and back-substitute
steps.why: ∫dt/(1+t) is the most basic log-form integral in the whole chapter — once the (1+t²) cancellation happens, no further algebra is needed before integrating.
common_mistakes: Missing the modulus bars on log|1+t|.
Forgetting to substitute tan(x/2) back in for t in the final line.
steps.memory_tip: The simplest tan(x/2) answers in this chapter end in a single log with tan(x/2) plugged straight in.
